Senses.Explanation: The eye faculty is the capacity through which visible form is encountered, distinguished in the records from the object seen and from visual consciousness. Masters and compilers examine whether it is identical with seeing, how it returns to the source, and what remains when root, object, and consciousness are cut off. The Source-Mirror Record distinguishes eye faculty, visible object, and visual consciousness, and describes the faculty as freely observing form. Feiyin Tongrong says that leaving even the eye faculty uncut shows the decisive cut has not occurred. A lamp-record answer says returning to the source through the eye faculty is named Manjusri. Across these uses the faculty is examined as a functional capacity, not reduced to the eyeball or to whatever is seen.
